body.name: Benchmark workflow
body.description: GitHub Actions workflow runs django-asv benchmarks on labeled pull requests, using asv continuous between HEAD^ and HEAD and failing the job on detected performance decreases.

sources.excerpt:
1: name: Benchmark
2: 
3: on:
4:   pull_request:
5:     types: [ labeled, synchronize, opened, reopened ]
6: 
7: permissions:
8:    contents: read
9: 
10: jobs:
11:   Run_benchmarks:
12:     if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'benchmark')
13:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
14:     timeout-minutes: 60
15:     steps:
16:       - name: Checkout Benchmark Repo
17:         uses: actions/checkout@v4
18:         with:
19:           repository: django/django-asv
20:           path: "."
21:           persist-credentials: false
22:       - name: Setup Miniforge
23:         # Pinned to v3.2.0.
24:         uses: conda-incubator/setup-miniconda@835234971496cad1653abb28a638a281cf32541f
25:         with:
26:           miniforge-version: "24.1.2-0"
27:           activate-environment: asv-bench
28:       - name: Install Requirements
29:         run: pip install -r requirements.txt
30:       - name: Cache Django
31:         uses: actions/cache@v3
32:         with:
33:           path: Django/*
34:           key: Django
35:       - name: Run Benchmarks
36:         shell: bash -l {0}
37:         run: |-
38:           asv machine --machine ubuntu-latest --yes > /dev/null
39:           echo 'Beginning benchmarks...'
40:           asv continuous --interleave-processes -a processes=2 --split --show-stderr 'HEAD^' 'HEAD' |\
41:           sed -n -E '/(before.*after.*ratio)|(BENCHMARKS)/,$p' >> out.txt
42:           echo 'Benchmarks Done.'
43:           echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
44:           cat out.txt >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
45:           echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
46:           if grep -q "PERFORMANCE DECREASED" out.txt;
47:           then
48:             exit 1
49:           fi

body.name: Cache middleware
body.description: Two-part middleware pair where FetchFromCacheMiddleware handles request-phase lookup and UpdateCacheMiddleware handles response-phase cache population and cache-key learning for eligible GET/HEAD responses.

1: """
2: Cache middleware. If enabled, each Django-powered page will be cached based on
3: URL. The canonical way to enable cache middleware is to set
4: ``UpdateCacheMiddleware`` as your first piece of middleware, and
5: ``FetchFromCacheMiddleware`` as the last::
6: 
7:     MIDDLEWARE = [
8:         'django.middleware.cache.UpdateCacheMiddleware',
9:         ...
10:         'django.middleware.cache.FetchFromCacheMiddleware'
11:     ]
12: 
13: This is counterintuitive, but correct: ``UpdateCacheMiddleware`` needs to run
14: last during the response phase, which processes middleware bottom-up;
15: ``FetchFromCacheMiddleware`` needs to run last during the request phase, which
16: processes middleware top-down.
17: 
18: The single-class ``CacheMiddleware`` can be used for some simple sites.
19: However, if any other piece of middleware needs to affect the cache key, you'll
20: need to use the two-part ``UpdateCacheMiddleware`` and
21: ``FetchFromCacheMiddleware``. This'll most often happen when you're using
22: Django's ``LocaleMiddleware``.
23: 
24: More details about how the caching works:
25: 
26: * Only GET or HEAD-requests with status code 200 are cached.
27: 
28: * The number of seconds each page is stored for is set by the "max-age" section
29:   of the response's "Cache-Control" header, falling back to the
30:   CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_SECONDS setting if the section was not found.
31: 
32: * This middleware expects that a HEAD request is answered with the same response
33:   headers exactly like the corresponding GET request.
34: 
35: * When a hit occurs, a shallow copy of the original response object is returned
36:   from process_request.
37: 
38: * Pages will be cached based on the contents of the request headers listed in
39:   the response's "Vary" header.
40: 
41: * This middleware also sets ETag, Last-Modified, Expires and Cache-Control
42:   headers on the response object.
43: 
44: * If the request had an Authorization header and the response was not marked
45:   "Cache-Control: public", the response will vary on Authorization.
46: """

32:         if not hasattr(request, "session"):

36:                 "insert "
37:                 "'django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware' before "
38:                 "'django.contrib.auth.middleware.AuthenticationMiddleware'."
39:             )

41:         request.auser = partial(auser, request)

46:     Middleware that redirects all unauthenticated requests to a login page.
47:

49:     """

51:     redirect_field_name = REDIRECT_FIELD_NAME
52: 
53:     def process_view(self, request, view_func, view_args, view_kwargs):
54:         if request.user.is_authenticated:
55:             return None
56: 
57:         if not getattr(view_func, "login_required", True):
58:             return None
59: 
60:         return self.handle_no_permission(request, view_func)
61: 
62:     def get_login_url(self, view_func):
63:         login_url = getattr(view_func, "login_url", None) or settings.LOGIN_URL
64:         if not login_url:
65:             raise ImproperlyConfigured(
66:                 "No login URL to redirect to. Define settings.LOGIN_URL or "
67:                 "provide a login_url via the 'django.contrib.auth.decorators."
68:                 "login_required' decorator."
69:             )
70:         return str(login_url)
71: 
72:     def get_redirect_field_name(self, view_func):
73:         return getattr(view_func, "redirect_field_name", self.redirect_field_name)
74:

76:         path = request.build_absolute_uri()

80:         login_scheme, login_netloc = urlsplit(resolved_login_url)[:2]

83:             not login_netloc or login_netloc == current_netloc

85:             path = request.get_full_path()

87:         return redirect_to_login(

91:         )

body.description: ModelSignal supports lazy sender resolution from app_label.ModelName strings and enables use_caching for common model lifecycle signals such as pre_save/post_save and m2m_changed.

1: """
2: Cache middleware. If enabled, each Django-powered page will be cached based on
3: URL. The canonical way to enable cache middleware is to set
4: ``UpdateCacheMiddleware`` as your first piece of middleware, and
5: ``FetchFromCacheMiddleware`` as the last::
6: 
7:     MIDDLEWARE = [
8:         'django.middleware.cache.UpdateCacheMiddleware',
9:         ...
10:         'django.middleware.cache.FetchFromCacheMiddleware'
11:     ]
12: 
13: This is counterintuitive, but correct: ``UpdateCacheMiddleware`` needs to run
14: last during the response phase, which processes middleware bottom-up;
15: ``FetchFromCacheMiddleware`` needs to run last during the request phase, which
16: processes middleware top-down.
17: 
18: The single-class ``CacheMiddleware`` can be used for some simple sites.
19: However, if any other piece of middleware needs to affect the cache key, you'll
20: need to use the two-part ``UpdateCacheMiddleware`` and
21: ``FetchFromCacheMiddleware``. This'll most often happen when you're using
22: Django's ``LocaleMiddleware``.
23: 
24: More details about how the caching works:
25: 
26: * Only GET or HEAD-requests with status code 200 are cached.
27: 
28: * The number of seconds each page is stored for is set by the "max-age" section
29:   of the response's "Cache-Control" header, falling back to the
30:   CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_SECONDS setting if the section was not found.
31: 
32: * This middleware expects that a HEAD request is answered with the same response
33:   headers exactly like the corresponding GET request.
34: 
35: * When a hit occurs, a shallow copy of the original response object is returned
36:   from process_request.
37: 
38: * Pages will be cached based on the contents of the request headers listed in
39:   the response's "Vary" header.
40: 
41: * This middleware also sets ETag, Last-Modified, Expires and Cache-Control
42:   headers on the response object.
43: 
44: * If the request had an Authorization header and the response was not marked
45:   "Cache-Control: public", the response will vary on Authorization.
46: """

48: import time

50: from django.conf import settings
51: from django.core.cache import DEFAULT_CACHE_ALIAS, caches
52: from django.utils.cache import (
53:     get_cache_key,
54:     get_max_age,
55:     has_vary_header,
56:     learn_cache_key,
57:     patch_response_headers,
58:     patch_vary_headers,
59: )
60: from django.utils.deprecation import MiddlewareMixin
61: from django.utils.http import parse_http_date_safe
62: 
63: 
64: class UpdateCacheMiddleware(MiddlewareMixin):
65:     """
66:     Response-phase cache middleware that updates the cache if the response is
67:     cacheable.
68: 
69:     Must be used as part of the two-part update/fetch cache middleware.
70:     UpdateCacheMiddleware must be the first piece of middleware in MIDDLEWARE
71:     so that it'll get called last during the response phase.
72:     """
73: 
74:     def __init__(self, get_response):
75:         super().__init__(get_response)
76:         self.cache_timeout = settings.CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_SECONDS
77:         self.page_timeout = None
78:         self.key_prefix = settings.CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_KEY_PREFIX
79:         self.cache_alias = settings.CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_ALIAS
80: 
81:     @property
82:     def cache(self):
83:         return caches[self.cache_alias]
84: 
85:     def _should_update_cache(self, request, response):
86:         return hasattr(request, "_cache_update_cache") and request._cache_update_cache
87: 
88:     def process_response(self, request, response):
89:         """Set the cache, if needed."""
90:         if not self._should_update_cache(request, response):
91:             # We don't need to update the cache, just return.
92:             return response
93: 
94:         if response.streaming or response.status_code not in (200, 304):
95:             return response
96: 
97:         # Don't cache responses that set a user-specific (and maybe security
98:         # sensitive) cookie while varying on Cookie.
99:         if response.cookies and has_vary_header(response, "Cookie"):
100:             return response

101: 
102:         # Don't cache responses when the Cache-Control header is set to
103:         # private, no-cache, or no-store.
104:         cache_control = response.get("Cache-Control", "").lower()
105:         if cache_control and any(
106:             directive in cache_control
107:             for directive in (
108:                 "private",
109:                 "no-cache",
110:                 "no-store",
111:             )
112:         ):
113:             return response
114: 
115:         # Don't cache responses when the Vary header contains '*'.
116:         if has_vary_header(response, "*"):
117:             return response
118: 
119:         # Page timeout takes precedence over the "max-age" and the default
120:         # cache timeout.
121:         timeout = self.page_timeout
122:         if timeout is None:
123:             # The timeout from the "max-age" section of the "Cache-Control"
124:             # header takes precedence over the default cache timeout.
125:             timeout = get_max_age(response)
126:             if timeout is None:
127:                 timeout = self.cache_timeout
128:             elif timeout == 0:
129:                 # max-age was set to 0, don't cache.
130:                 return response
131:         patch_response_headers(response, timeout)
132:         # Make the response vary on Authorization if the request bears that
133:         # header, unless allowed by "public" per RFC 9111, Section 3.5. No
134:         # exceptions are made for "s-maxage" and "must-revalidate" since these
135:         # are not currently implemented by Django.
136:         if request.headers.get("Authorization") and "public" not in cache_control:
137:             patch_vary_headers(response, ("Authorization",))
138:         if timeout and response.status_code == 200:
139:             cache_key = learn_cache_key(
140:                 request, response, timeout, self.key_prefix, cache=self.cache
141:             )
142:             if hasattr(response, "render") and callable(response.render):
143:                 response.add_post_render_callback(
144:                     lambda r: self.cache.set(cache_key, r, timeout)
145:                 )
146:             else:
147:                 self.cache.set(cache_key, response, timeout)
148:         return response

151: class FetchFromCacheMiddleware(MiddlewareMixin):
152:     """
153:     Request-phase cache middleware that fetches a page from the cache.
154: 
155:     Must be used as part of the two-part update/fetch cache middleware.
156:     FetchFromCacheMiddleware must be the last piece of middleware in MIDDLEWARE
157:     so that it'll get called last during the request phase.
158:     """
159: 
160:     def __init__(self, get_response):
161:         super().__init__(get_response)
162:         self.key_prefix = settings.CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_KEY_PREFIX
163:         self.cache_alias = settings.CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_ALIAS
164: 
165:     @property
166:     def cache(self):
167:         return caches[self.cache_alias]
168: 
169:     def process_request(self, request):
170:         """
171:         Check whether the page is already cached and return the cached
172:         version if available.
173:         """
174:         if request.method not in ("GET", "HEAD"):
175:             request._cache_update_cache = False
176:             return None  # Don't bother checking the cache.
177: 
178:         # try and get the cached GET response
179:         cache_key = get_cache_key(request, self.key_prefix, "GET", cache=self.cache)
180:         if cache_key is None:
181:             request._cache_update_cache = True
182:             return None  # No cache information available, need to rebuild.
183:         response = self.cache.get(cache_key)
184:         # if it wasn't found and we are looking for a HEAD, try looking just for that
185:         if response is None and request.method == "HEAD":
186:             cache_key = get_cache_key(
187:                 request, self.key_prefix, "HEAD", cache=self.cache
188:             )
189:             response = self.cache.get(cache_key)
190: 
191:         if response is None:
192:             request._cache_update_cache = True
193:             return None  # No cache information available, need to rebuild.
194: 
195:         # Derive the age estimation of the cached response.
196:         if (max_age_seconds := get_max_age(response)) is not None and (
197:             expires_timestamp := parse_http_date_safe(response["Expires"])
198:         ) is not None:
199:             now_timestamp = int(time.time())
200:             remaining_seconds = expires_timestamp - now_timestamp

finding.statement: Within the scoped sources there is no benchmark or numeric measurement isolating middleware CPU overhead apart from backend cache I/O, so the claim that this extra work is materially expensive remains unmeasured.
finding.workload: Benchmarking UpdateCacheMiddleware miss-path cost excluding backend latency.
finding.falsification: Falsified by scoped benchmark data reporting miss-path middleware cost or a benchmark fixture specifically measuring cache middleware internals without backend I/O.

evaluation.reason: The scoped source supports the mechanism claim as stated. FetchFromCacheMiddleware sets request._cache_update_cache = True on ordinary GET/HEAD misses both when no learned cache metadata exists and when a lookup misses, making the response-side update path part of the normal miss contract rather than a narrow exception (0dbb31983a4147fcb66d983d83ce5088). UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response then performs multiple non-backend steps before storing: it checks whether update is needed, rejects streaming and non-200/304 responses, rejects cookie+Vary and Cache-Control private/no-cache/no-store cases, rejects Vary: *, computes timeout from page timeout/max-age/default, patches response headers, may patch Vary on Authorization, and on timeout with status 200 calls learn_cache_key() before cache.set() (262dfc01049b4ef9a55d5c58fc7e678d, 0dbb31983a4147fcb66d983d83ce5088). Unchanged cache tests show learn_cache_key()/get_cache_key behavior is expected contract machinery, not a rare edge path: get_cache_key() returns None before learning and stable keys after learning, including Vary-derived, i18n, timezone, host, and query-string-sensitive behavior (7558a64d33b140e8847d14bc6b19c261, 00ebc77081d5410c961cc0967b38dcf7, 5e058eab0b684ee7924bcb0ce4d918ff, 61f05c08b28549e6969580e484c9b4df). No contrary scoped test evidence shows these checks are usually bypassed; tests/middleware/tests.py has no UpdateCacheMiddleware references and only generic cache-related header tests by literal search (6d57c81161fb451899adb217173b8c60, ec50f5a31ba44b6db9c3d600a6f3dac2). The benchmark workflow is generic ASV execution and does not provide a numeric measurement isolating miss-path middleware CPU cost excluding backend I/O, so only the existence of repeated work is supported here, not material impact magnitude (9219e51ca4bb487ab4904098dfaceb45). The falsification criterion is not met because the logic is neither shown to be narrow nor bypassed on ordinary cacheable misses, and parts of it are explicitly aligned with the middleware contract documented in source comments/docstring (262dfc01049b4ef9a55d5c58fc7e678d).
evaluation.feedback: Keep the claim bounded to demonstrated source behavior: ordinary cacheable GET/HEAD misses do execute repeated response-side gating/header/key-learning work before storage. Do not upgrade that into a verified performance regression without a benchmark that isolates middleware CPU from backend cache latency and view cost.
non_blocking_uncertainties: The hypothesis says overhead is 'potentially material'; scope supports potential repeated work but not measured materiality.
Tests establish contract and key-learning semantics, not how often various Vary/header combinations occur in real workloads.
Authorization-related Vary patching is conditional, so not every ordinary miss pays that specific branch even though the broader response-side checks still run.

uncertainties: No numeric measurement in scope shows whether the non-I/O miss-path work is material relative to view rendering or real cache backend latency.
The benchmark workflow exists, but the scoped workflow file only shows generic ASV execution and not a cache-middleware-specific benchmark.
The tests demonstrate required semantics of key learning and Vary-sensitive behavior, but they do not quantify how often different Vary/header combinations occur in production workloads.

spec.hypothesis: The existing benchmark workflow can detect regressions only if django-asv contains benchmarks for cache middleware, auth middleware, or signal dispatch; absent such benchmarks, optimization ideas here lack repository-supported measurement coverage.
spec.falsification: Inspect django-asv benchmark definitions or workflow references proving these paths are benchmarked already.
spec.rationale: The workflow proves benchmarking infrastructure exists and runs HEAD^ vs HEAD, but it does not identify benchmark contents. This matters because code-level suspicions remain unmeasured.

opportunities.title: Check whether auth middleware laziness is contradicted by downstream contracts rather than being an avoidable overhead source

spec.title: Check whether auth middleware laziness is contradicted by downstream contracts rather than being an avoidable overhead source
spec.hypothesis: Base AuthenticationMiddleware itself is intentionally low-overhead because it only installs lazy accessors; meaningful per-request auth cost is instead forced by downstream consumers like LoginRequiredMiddleware evaluating request.user.is_authenticated, so replacing the lazy wrapper in the middleware would contradict existing execution contracts.
spec.falsification: Inspect auth middleware tests and remaining source to find code paths where AuthenticationMiddleware eagerly resolves the user on every request, or explicit tests/contracts allowing a non-lazy request.user interface.
spec.rationale: The code clearly caches get_user() only on first access via SimpleLazyObject and separately shows LoginRequiredMiddleware immediately touching request.user.is_authenticated. That supports laziness as a contract and shifts suspicion to consumers, but unchanged tests were not yet examined.

opportunities.title: Validate cache-middleware miss-path overhead from repeated cache-key learning and header inspection

spec.title: Validate cache-middleware miss-path overhead from repeated cache-key learning and header inspection
spec.hypothesis: In cacheable GET/HEAD miss paths, UpdateCacheMiddleware does nontrivial per-response work beyond backend set(), including cookie/vary checks and learn_cache_key(), making middleware overhead material even before cache backend cost is considered.
spec.falsification: Inspect the remaining body of django/middleware/cache.py and any nearby tests/benchmarks to show that learn_cache_key() is only reached in narrow exceptional cases, or that contracts/tests explicitly assert negligible/no extra work on normal misses.
spec.rationale: Observed code confirms response-side gating, cookie/vary checks, and a call site for learn_cache_key(). This is a plausible avoidable overhead candidate, but impact is unmeasured and the exact normal-path frequency/contracts were not fully read.

opportunities.title: Confirm whether signal-dispatch receiver lookup is already optimized by caching, weakening the case for dispatcher-level micro-optimization

spec.title: Confirm whether signal-dispatch receiver lookup is already optimized by caching, weakening the case for dispatcher-level micro-optimization
spec.hypothesis: For model lifecycle signals, use_caching=True already reduces repeated receiver-resolution overhead, so a generic claim that signal dispatch is an avoidable hot-path bottleneck is weakened unless django.dispatch.dispatcher shows remaining per-send synchronization or cache invalidation costs.
spec.falsification: Inspect django.dispatch.dispatcher and relevant tests to show either that use_caching does not affect send-time receiver lookup materially, or that contracts require expensive lazy resolution/disconnect behavior on hot paths.
spec.rationale: The code directly shows use_caching=True on core model signals, which contradicts the simpler alternative explanation that receiver lookup is wholly uncached. The real remaining cost may be elsewhere, but dispatcher internals were not read.

spec.question: Across cache middleware, auth middleware, and signal-dispatch paths, which code-supported mechanisms most plausibly create avoidable per-request overhead or reliability-sensitive work, and which alternatives are contradicted by the existing execution contracts/tests?

spec.question: Does Django's signal dispatcher still impose avoidable per-send overhead on model lifecycle signals despite use_caching=True, or do dispatcher internals and unchanged tests falsify that hypothesis and instead show the cost is already constrained by contract?
spec.hypothesis: For model lifecycle signals, dispatcher send-time receiver resolution is already materially optimized by sender-based caching in django/dispatch/dispatcher.py, so a broad claim that signal dispatch is an avoidable hot-path bottleneck should be falsified unless tests or code reveal unavoidable repeated full receiver scans or synchronization on normal sends.
spec.falsification: This hypothesis is false if dispatcher.py or tests/dispatch/tests.py show that normal send() operations for cached model signals still re-scan all receivers, frequently miss the sender cache, or perform required per-send synchronization/cleanup work that defeats caching on the common path.

spec.question: In Django's cache middleware, does the normal cacheable GET/HEAD miss path perform avoidable repeated work beyond backend cache I/O, or do source and unchanged tests show the extra header/key-learning logic is limited or required by contract?
spec.hypothesis: On cacheable GET/HEAD misses, django/middleware/cache.py performs additional per-response work such as cacheability checks, Vary/header inspection, and learn_cache_key() that is routinely executed before storing the response, making middleware overhead potentially material even when backend cache latency is excluded.
spec.falsification: This hypothesis is false if the source and unchanged tests show that learn_cache_key() and related header-inspection/gating logic run only in narrow exceptional cases, are commonly bypassed on ordinary cacheable misses, or are explicitly required and already minimized by the middleware contract.
